args: Analyze php-src/Zend/zend_operators.c div_function(), especially its slow scalar-conversion retry and div_by_zero cleanup when result == op1. What is the safest root-cause fix, and are there analogous arithmetic functions or established cleanup patterns nearby that should guide the patch?

The provided ASan report shows an in-place `/=` operation with a refcounted numeric string left operand. div_function() converts operands, destroys op1 before retrying, the retry detects a zero divisor, and div_by_zero only sets result undefined if result != op1. The stale in-place zval then gets copied by ZEND_ASSIGN_OP and zend_gc_addref reads freed string storage. I am considering either marking op1/result UNDEF immediately after its destructor in the conversion path, or changing div_by_zero to always make result undefined while ensuring no live value leaks and avoiding destruction of stale storage. I need source-aware guidance on semantics and analogous implementations.
